edited_fraction: 0.016% (rebuilt published Qwen3.5-0.8B edit); one unit for the Claude Opus 5.5 edit; whole network for MinAtar/Go writes
cost_reported: inference only: the edited thinking-mode model uses 4.8-10.7x the tokens per answer of the unedited default model (117 vs 22 correct answers per million tokens on MATH-500); no editor cost
evidence_notes: A replication and critique of the MIT WSP post (PAPER.md). Weight writes are single replies without tools (MinAtar, reading) or Codex Python with tools disabled (Exp. 3, 4, 6), all without feedback, so direct_values plus code_or_tensor_tool and open_loop. Default mode alone reaches 74-89% of the published gain and the edit adds 0.0 +/- 1.25 points there (inference-only fix). Game identification follows a row-length decoy 20/20 (layout fallback); the car edit works on all-zero weights and a two-step script solves the task; Astra succeeded 1/10 on new car attempts. GSM8K was subsampled. No preregistration. The pages contain only PAPER.md and reviews, which cite results/eval files but give no code link, so release is coded no. Authors are not named; the attached reviews suggest an agent pipeline, but the paper does not say so (unclear).
